en.Hilly is the middle step. Gentle gives t: Hilly is the middle step. Gentle gives the most flat land, higher is steeper. Snow from about 330 m: Alpine's peaks reach it from Gentle, the highest hills of most other map types from Hilly.
en.One continuous mountain belt (snow from: One continuous mountain belt (snow from Hilly up) with two graded passes and foothills; sea on one side or none.
en.Snow-capped massifs scattered over high: Snow-capped massifs scattered over high ground, valleys between them and two graded passes; sea on one side or none.
Where the map type's main feature goes. Random: the seed decides. None: no sea.
en.No sea: the land goes on where the sea w: No sea: the land goes on where the sea would be, and the rivers leave the map there.
en.Where the big river ends: in the sea, on: Where the big river ends: in the sea, on the edge opposite where it comes from. None: no sea; the river leaves the map there.
en.Fewer tree models for lower-spec compute: Fewer tree models for lower-spec computers (about half). Where forests grow stays the same; only how many trees are placed changes.
en.Apply to map waits for this preview, the: Apply to map waits for this preview, then applies it.
en.How high the whole land rises: hills, mo: How high the whole land rises: hills, mountains and plateaus together. Lower it for flatter land that is easier for railways and roads; raise it for higher, steeper land with more snow on the peaks. 0 % gives almost flat land.
en.How many lakes form along the rivers (up: How many lakes form along the rivers (up to 300 %). Lakes need natural hollows, so above 100 % a map may have no room for more; the Report then says so. 0 % gives no lakes apart from small oxbow lakes beside river bends.
en.How many rivers and streams the map gets: How many rivers and streams the map gets. Above 100 % smaller valleys get their own streams, so there are more rivers reaching further up into the hills; below 100 % only the larger rivers are left. The Water setting sets the starting amount.
en.How much of the land is hill country: pa: How much of the land is hill country: patches of hills a few kilometres across, with lower, open land between them. Lower it for more open land for towns and railways; raise it for more hills (at 200 % nearly all the land). How tall the hills are is Hill height.
en.How much the rivers wind. 0 % gives almo: How much the rivers wind. 0 % gives almost straight rivers that follow the valley's gentle curve, easy to run a railway beside; raise it for wide, looping bends.
en.How ragged the coastline is: coves, head: How ragged the coastline is: coves, headlands and small bays. Lower it for a smoother, straighter coast; raise it for a more jagged one. No effect on maps without sea.
en.How tall the hills in the hill country a: How tall the hills in the hill country are. Lower it for low, gentle hills that roads and railways cross easily; raise it for tall, steep hills. Where the hills are and how much land they cover stays the same (that is Hill country).
en.How wide the flat valley floors along th: How wide the flat valley floors along the rivers are. Wider valleys give more flat land beside the rivers for towns, stations and railways; at 0 % the valleys are narrow with steep sides.
en.Makes the preview for the current settin: Makes the preview for the current settings first (as Preview does), then puts that map on your map.
en.Puts the previewed map on your map. Fore: Puts the previewed map on your map. Forests and biomes are added now; the preview shows the land only.
en.Ridges and gullies running down the slop: Ridges and gullies running down the slopes, as if carved by rain over a long time; the steeper the slope, the deeper they are. Flat land gets none. 0 % turns them off for smooth slopes; raise it for rugged hillsides.
en.Run test stopped: the settings changed d: Run test stopped: the settings changed during the test (see the saved log).
en.Settings changed since the last Preview:: Settings changed since the last Preview: nothing applied.
en.Settings changed while the preview was b: Settings changed while the preview was being made: nothing applied. Press Apply to map again.
en.Small bumps a few metres high on hills a: Small bumps a few metres high on hills and slopes, so they look natural rather than smooth. Plains, valley floors and beaches get none, so they stay easy to build on. Lower it for smoother hills, raise it for rougher, rockier ground.
en.The preview did not finish (see the log): The preview did not finish (see the log): nothing applied. The buttons work again.
en.Which way the strait runs. East-West: fr: Which way the strait runs. East-West: from the west edge to the east edge, with land to the north and south. North-South: with land to the west and east. Diagonal: from near one corner to near the opposite one, along the long side (on a map three or more times as long as wide, or under about 3 km across, it runs nearly straight: only a few degrees off the long side). Random: the seed decides.
en.A sea strait splits the map from edge to: A sea strait splits the map from edge to edge: wide sounds for ships and ferries, a few narrows for bridges, flat shores on both sides.
en.The Studio window cannot open safely: an: The Studio window cannot open safely: another mod replaced the game's window component and the game's own one was not found. Disable mods that change game windows, then load the map again.

en.Hilly is the middle step. Gentle gives t: Hilly is the middle step. Gentle gives the most flat land, higher is steeper. Snow from about 210 m: Alpine, Mountain Range and Highland Plateau reach it from Gentle, most other map types from Moderate; Island Chain and Rolling Plains only a few peaks from Rugged; Delta Lowlands hardly ever (at most a spot at Mountainous).
